mechanism: exact number-theoretic identity (n^2 mod 4 = n mod 2) + parity phase kickback on a clean ancilla, with an explicit near-pi/2 angle match that absorbs the IR's rounding of pi/2 into the exact 1e-6 budget

rule.name: kerr_half_pi_parity_kickback_angle_tolerant_5op
rule.idea: Exact identity n^2 mod 4 = n mod 2 turns exp(-i(pi/2)n^2) into a parity-dependent phase diag(1,-i,1,-i,...). A clean ancilla is put in |+> via H, CR(pi) = (-iZ)^n kicks back parity p=(-1)^n onto the ancilla's Z eigenvalue, rx(phi) on the ancilla multiplies by exp(-i(phi/2)p), CR(-pi) un-kicks and H restores the ancilla to |0>, factorising out exactly and leaving exp(-i(phi/2)p) on the mode. theta = pi/2 + k*pi + delta is handled by matching phi = -pi/2 + 3*delta (absorbing the -delta*(3/2)p piece of the n<=3 expansion n^2 = 3n - p n + (3/2)p - 3/2 exactly) and emitting R(k*pi) on the mode only when k is odd; the residual exp(-i delta(3n - p n)) is bounded by about 3|delta| in operator distance on the verified truncated subspace and is well under the 1e-6 exact contract, so it is charged nothing against the eps ledger. This removes the IR's rounding of pi/2 as an obstacle: a tight exact-equality predicate would reject theta = 1.5707963 (delta = theta - pi/2 ~= -2.68e-8) even though it is physically pi/2.
